body: Added an optional silent persistent status notification that shows whether Switchly is enabled and which profile is selected.
Added a direct Profiles action to the status notification and kept its state synchronized with manual, scheduled, temporary, NFC, QR, barcode, profile, boot, and app-start changes.
Added a dedicated System status section under Feature access and requests Android notification permission when the feature is enabled.
Fixed the Website rules globe icon and restored the read-only confirmation shown before opening Rules while Switchly protection is active.
Expanded Switchly overview with Active time, Opens, Blocks, and Limits reached for every supported statistics range.
Clarified App & website usage with consistent Opens and Blocks labels, and fixed open counts so internal Activity changes are not counted as separate app opens.
Organized Activity into Statistics & events and Review sections, aligned the Active time icon, and standardized Website rules on the Language/globe icon.
Standardized layout section spacing and XML formatting, and normalized all vector drawable files to one predictable structure with documented exceptions.
Fixed NFC dispatch for UID-only, read-only, blank, and non-matching NDEF tags by declaring NFC technologies as alternative TECH_DISCOVERED matches instead of requiring every technology at once.

Refined Hidden apps and Usage exclusions by recognizing Google Settings as a suggestion, excluding legacy permission-controller and Android System Intelligence components, and matching only the current Switchly application ID.

Polished 2.2.3 backup and status UX with visible cloud-loading progress, selectable notification detail levels, read-only Quick Action access, visible usage metric chips, corrected language/website icons, and reliable statistics-database restore.

Improved NFC writing with background I/O, retryable tag-loss handling, direct UID fallback that keeps the selected action and profile, safe rewrite flows for paired tags, and protection against immediate post-write re-triggering.
Enhanced the optional status notification with the active session timer and the selected profile’s configured blocked or allowed app count.
Refined usage insights with consistent info actions, a clearer App usage details layout, and usage-time, Opens, and Blocks chips for every supported range, including custom ranges.

Fixed legacy statistics restore by normalizing old numeric preference types, moving archived counters back to their canonical storage, preserving them across the database restore phase, and mirroring the merged result into the durable statistics archive.
Reduced App & website usage loading work by calculating Opens and Blocks for all visible apps in bulk, and avoided unnecessary profile/app-count reads for compact status-notification modes.
Renamed Home, widgets & shortcuts to Widgets & shortcuts and fixed Feature access so the System status controls are actually visible.
Redesigned Support as a central help and diagnostics screen, moved the live log viewer out of Developer tools, and made recent logs directly viewable or copyable without unlocking Developer mode.

Refined Permissions with a compact Issues/OK toolbar status and clearer re-check feedback, fixed forced onboarding to return to Help & about, grouped the Switchly Store directly above Other Switchly apps under Info, removed the unused Troubleshooting screen, opened Developer tools directly with a compact topbar mode toggle, polished the Support report dialog, and corrected 2.2.2 to appear as a beta release.
Added a compatibility warning before restoring older or different backup formats and clarified that Switchly performs a best-effort migration for compatible legacy counters.
Made uninstall protection independent from app access lock, with PIN or biometric confirmation before it can be disabled in Switchly.

Improved navigation and shortcut reliability: Rules now open directly in read-only mode during active or temporary protection, bottom-navigation destinations switch without animating the entire screen, launcher scanner shortcuts reliably return to the existing Switchly task, and Home uses one shared camera action for choosing QR or barcode scanning.
Fixed Emergency Unlock in locked and schedule-only setups: blocking pauses reliably while active, protected Settings and Rules stay read-only, and schedules stay paused until the bypass ends.
Stopped repeated schedule checks from re-applying an unchanged state or profile, preventing duplicate vibrations, notifications, and noisy schedule logs.

Prevented transient schedule permission warnings after device wake or Accessibility-service reconnects by accepting the configured service state during startup and re-checking permissions before opening the repair screen.
Reduced false Accessibility warnings during device wake-up, service reconnects, and app updates by verifying the service state before notifying.

Stabilized Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and location schedule monitors during app launch, boot, permission changes, and rapid rule edits, preventing foreground-service startup timeouts and stale or lost geofence registrations.
Added Temporary enable and Temporary pause directly to Home for the selected profile, with clearer Protection status labels for normal and temporary states.

Closed protection bypasses during Temporary pause, Emergency Unlock, and active protection: Rules open directly in read-only mode and Settings remain reviewable, while protection-sensitive controls and every Rules edit stay locked until Switchly is fully disabled.

Closed a Keys & codes bypass by locking QR creation, payload viewing, copying and sharing, plus barcode setup and editing, while Switchly is active; existing QR and barcode scanners remain available for their intended control actions.
Fixed the missing Switchly icon in Android's Quick Settings tile setup dialog and marked tile setup rows as external system actions.

Improved NFC setup with clearer written-action versus UID-only pairing guidance, system NFC warnings, paired-tag empty states, info dialogs, expanded scan diagnostics, and reliable per-tag daily/cooldown limits for Disable, disabling Toggle, Temporary disable and Re-entry actions. Paired tags now use the same structured profile, action, duration and limit setup as managed barcodes; writable tags can keep the profile, action and duration stored on the tag or override them, including ask-when-scanned temporary actions. QR and barcode code limits follow the same unlock-only rules without counting enable actions, profile switches or no-op scans.

Kept QR and barcode scanners directly accessible from Home, Quick Settings, widgets, and shortcuts even while App lock protects the rest of Switchly, and removed duplicate scanner shortcuts from Settings.

Allowed protected apps such as the Google app to be blocked after an explicit risk warning; Switchly remains excluded from app rules, while its visibility in Usage & Insights can be controlled through a consistently accent-themed Hidden apps screen, and bulk or automatic selection still skips protected apps.

Redesigned Home customization around draggable main cards and collapsible nested contents: Protection Control keeps status, enable/disable, profile, temporary actions and Emergency Unlock together, while app selection stays in the dedicated managed-app card. Quick Actions now reflow without gaps and let a final unpaired tile span the full row; the redundant Blocked right now module was removed.

Refined onboarding with an immediate loading state and cached seven-day usage preview, selectable Default, Custom, Simple, or Advanced Home layouts, plus individual optional setup pages with live status cards, direct Home-mode selection, focused shortcut and feature-access controls, and direct background-access and device-specific help. The post-onboarding navigation tour now highlights both the icon and label of exactly one destination at a time, while the managed-app list starts collapsed.

Polished profiles, paired tags, schedules, and rule screens with a cleaner profile editor, better empty states, direct add actions, consistent profile context in App, Website, and In-app rules, clearer per-schedule profile targeting, and consistent Info, Cancel, and Delete selection controls; enabled Developer mode now also appears directly in Settings.

Improved Website and In-app rules with clearer rows, checkbox-based pausing, direct limit actions, and active-state highlighting for mode and usage toggles; added a Brave Shields fallback that continues using the last confirmed domain when URL accessibility data temporarily disappears.

Added best-effort Website rule support for links opened inside Facebook Messenger’s built-in browser, while requiring a detected browser/WebView surface so normal chats and message text are not treated as website activity.

Made Activity History independent from diagnostic logs, stored it in persistent per-day buckets, simplified Activity into one consistently ordered list, kept blocked notifications read-only while active, and added a Switchly overview for scans, state changes, schedules, Temporary enables, and Emergency Unlocks. Today remains free while longer ranges remain Premium.

Expanded Switchly overview with range-based App launches and Blocks totals, unified segmented controls across App, Website, In-app, Hidden-app and Usage screens, and fixed a Hidden apps crash caused by themes without colorOutline.

Separated App, Website, and In-app Block selected/Allow selected modes per profile, and preserved case-sensitive Android package names in Hidden apps so apps such as Amazon Shopping appear consistently in both Usage & Insights and App pickers.
Added Suggested labels to the Hidden apps App picker and replaced scattered deprecated PackageManager suppressions with one typed API compatibility layer.

Moved long-range statistics into a durable local Room archive while keeping the existing stores as a fast compatibility cache; daily counters, Activity History, website and unlock sessions, and exact app sessions now survive Android UsageEvents expiry and are included in local JSON and chunked cloud backup/restore.

Added Hidden apps under Settings > Personalization with separate Usage & Insights and App pickers lists. Usage filters remove selected apps from top apps, summaries, launch counts, timelines, and onboarding insights without changing raw history; app-picker filters hide apps only when adding new selections, while existing profile entries, limits, and configured rules remain visible and editable.
Showed today's Active time sessions and activity details directly instead of hiding them behind a separate Today row.
Reduced repeated Billing, backup, restore, and duplicate diagnostic logs, and replaced long explanatory toasts with clearer inline status, snackbars, or dialogs.

Improved App lock and uninstall-protection guidance, warnings, setup actions, and support diagnostics for Device Admin, Emergency Unlock, and optional Device Owner protection; App lock now shows its live state directly below the screen title, and the Support screen uses clearer contact and report actions.

Clarified that usage and statistics stay local unless explicitly exported, backed up, or included in a support report, updated the Privacy & data export selector, and refreshed Help Center guidance for permanent statistics, read-only protection, Premium support options, and official 3D-printed Switchly tags.

Added dedicated GitLab and Discord brand icons, removed disconnected legacy statistics code and unused dependencies/resources, and completed Android 16 edge-to-edge, NFC preference, manifest, layout-depth, and stale-code cleanup.

Redesigned onboarding with aligned hero sizing and vertical spacing, a simpler two-point welcome and app-picking flow, a two-card private Usage Access explanation, a reliable icon-based 7-day Top 7 report, and a clear linear finish: selected key/code and schedule guidance stays in the main flow, Home customization is the penultimate step, and Ready to start completes setup. The welcome step now has a clear Start badge, and a short first-run coach tour highlights Home, Rules, Activity and Settings after setup instead of placing navigation guidance at the bottom of the final page. Required onboarding steps now also block forward swipe navigation until completed, the first-run navigation tour uses a clear dimmed coach dialog in the center of the screen and visibly accents each matching bottom-navigation destination, while the 2.2.2 feedback notice is suppressed after both completing and skipping onboarding and waits until a later normal app launch. The complete permission overview still requires Accessibility and Usage Access before activation, and the redundant Activity Home quick action was removed now that Activity is always available in the bottom navigation.
Separated official signed release packaging from public unsigned validation builds so public repository builds remain reproducible without private signing files.
Refined icon semantics across App lock, Activity History, support, QR sharing, and Quick Settings setup, including clearer PIN, biometric, send, share, and completed-state icons.

Normalized vector drawable structure around the shared 960 × 960 icon viewport, added a dedicated Hidden apps visibility icon, and removed permanently hidden App picker, Home setup, Premium, In-app, and info-screen UI remnants together with their unused code and strings.
Reorganized bottom navigation to use Activity instead of Insights, with direct entries for active time, usage statistics, app launches, screen unlocks, activity history, and blocked notifications.
Renamed the NFC, QR, barcode, and paired-tag management area to Keys & codes for clearer wording and consistent screen titles.
Kept QR and barcode quick scanners reachable from Keys & codes after removing them from the Rules hub.
Kept Rules focused on profile rules such as apps, websites, in-app rules, and schedules.
Moved Emergency unlock into the Permissions & reliability area of Settings as a dedicated safety action after the Activity navigation cleanup.
Clarified App lock versus uninstall protection with a new Settings hint, Advanced/ADB guidance, FAQ wording, and support-report status details.
Improved profile handling so newly created profiles update their active state immediately.
Made In-app and Website rules profile-aware, including safer migration of older global rule settings.
Added Block selected and Allow selected modes to In-app and Website rules.
Cleaned up In-app rule controls and wording so Block/Allow behavior is easier to understand.
Removed YouTube Home from selectable In-app rules while keeping Shorts, Subscriptions, You, mini-player, and picture-in-picture rules.
Updated In-app rule availability labels for YouTube, Instagram, X, and Snapchat.
Improved YouTube Shorts blocking when Shorts are opened from the Home feed.
Reduced YouTube false positives by separating Shorts, mini-player, and picture-in-picture cleanup paths.
Prevented retry probes, stale Shorts hints, and mini-player cleanup from creating false Shorts blocks.
Reduced Shorts/Home redirect loops with safer YouTube Home navigation during cleanup.
Updated Premium wording to focus on unlocked features such as custom ranges, statistics insights, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and location schedules.
Expanded FAQ content for profile-scoped rules, Block selected/Allow selected behavior, supported In-app apps, and Website rule modes.
Kept extended statistics ranges, custom ranges, and detailed drill-downs behind Premium.
Added live Activity History refresh with clearer action, profile, source, duration, filter, sort, and custom range details.
Improved Activity History layout with inline time ranges, full-width custom ranges, and shared Statistics filter styling.
Expanded Activity with Active time, Activity History, App usage, Website usage, blocked-notification insights, app launches, screen unlocks, and timeline-style detail views.
Added shared date-range controls, profile-scoped filters, custom date ranges, and clearer statistics filter popups across Activity screens.
Improved App usage and Website usage detail headers with clearer screen titles and prominent app/domain names.
Added per-domain Website Rule toggles so individual domains can be enabled or disabled directly from the list.
Polished Website rule entries with the same card background, border, ripple, and spacing used across Switchly lists.
Defaulted new Website rules to Always instead of Daily limit.
Removed the inline edit icon from Website rule rows while keeping row tap and swipe edit available.
Added enable/disable switches for individual paired NFC tags so tags can be paused without removing them.
Added an empty state for In-app rules when no supported apps are installed.
Changed Website and In-app rules to work without separate master toggles; configured rules now apply directly.
Added backup and restore coverage for Activity History, Website rules, 2.2 settings, profile rules, usage statistics, limits, and Wi-Fi preferences.
Added restore category selection, restore previews, backup metadata, progress dialogs, and a local Privacy & Data screen with export and deletion actions.
Added Switchly Store links and improved official tag setup flows for NFC, QR, barcode, and paired tags.
Improved NFC, QR, barcode, and paired-tag setup with launch guidance, setup status handling, and hardware-aware permission controls.
Added schedule overlap warnings, conflict detection, compact active schedule details, and detailed schedule event logs.
Fixed NFC/manual disables being immediately overwritten by the same active schedule while still allowing other matching schedules to take over.
Improved Customize Home and Quick Actions with long-press drag reorder, restore-default actions, clearer card-style rows, and independent ordering for the contents inside Protection Control.
Added an optional onboarding usage report that can summarize distracting apps and add them to the current profile.
Added blocker explanation popups, pause-until shortcuts, schedule priority guidance, and richer support-report context.
Improved shared screen styling across schedules, blocked notifications, editable lists, dialogs, paired tags, barcodes, profiles, websites, in-app rules, and statistics.
Improved Home and Activity navigation so active timers only appear while Switchly is active and App usage stays in Activity.

Fixed Premium purchase launch handling for concurrent Billing connection requests, disconnected or stalled Google Play flows, duplicate attempts, and already-owned purchases, and added consistent restricted access: Settings and Rules remain viewable while protection-sensitive controls are read-only, with Premium, Emergency unlock, Appearance, Account & Data, and Help still reachable.
Fixed trusted NFC, QR, and barcode action dispatch hardening and kept runtime/security-only state out of backups.
Fixed website edit/detail lock handling, Android 11/OEM install-check crashes, quick limit dialog compatibility, and selected-count dialog title issues.
Fixed Wi-Fi/Bluetooth trigger foreground-service startup races, missing-permission handling, and silent trigger/protection notification behavior.
Fixed startup ANR risk by deferring shortcut, trigger, policy, Play Integrity, and usage-stat binder work away from the main thread.
Fixed onboarding permission return behavior, support email visibility, editor actions, swipe actions, popup Cancel behavior, obsolete resource cleanup, and Material date picker theme handling.
Fixed custom temporary duration input so manual minute values support the same 24-hour maximum as NFC/QR temporary actions.
Major 2.2.0 update with a reworked setup experience, cleaner controls, improved usage insights, and many UX fixes

Reworked Blocking Controls into clearer control modes, feature access, channels, and mode-based setup guidance
Improved App Picker, profile creation/editing, app-list editing, active-profile highlighting, and selected-app review flows

Improved website blocking display and website/domain detection feedback

Improved Blocked notifications with equal filter chips, app icons, clearer filter/sort behavior, better details, and empty states

Improved foreground/blocking reliability by hardening blocking flows and moving shortcut refresh work off the main thread

Fixed Temporary Enable behavior when started while Switchly was already enabled

Improved Wi-Fi schedule reliability with safer SSID refresh, reconnect handling, and diagnostics
